newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares revive late on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares revive late on bargain hunting.

text.p: Singapore shares recovered to end slightly firmer on Monday, supported by bargain hunting after a slide triggered by Fraser & Neave results.
Soft drinks company F&N depressed the early market after posting a fall of 18 percent in half year profits on Friday.
"The market was livelier in the afternoon due to emergence of foreign funds, but blue chips are still weak," a remisier said, noting there were few calls to buy Singapore stocks.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) rose 0.96 points to 1,991.08 at the close on a moderate turnover of 169 million shares. But losers outpaced gainers by 239 to 85.
Activity was mainly dominated by recently listed issues and small capitalisation counters, dealers said.

Debut stock Australand, active in the early market, was overtaken in volume by Guthrie when 32 million shares were crossed at Singapore $0.60. Dealers said they were not aware of any news or rumours resulting in the trades.

F&N struck a new low at S$10, down 30 cents, after announcing its results. City Development eased S$0.20 to $13.60 and foreign tranches of some banks. DBS dropped 20 cents to S$18 and OCBC fell 20 cents to $15.
